hints: Set discriminant $\Delta = (2 - m)^2 - 36 > 0$ for two distinct intersections.
Factorise $(m + 4)(m - 8) > 0$ and state the outside intervals.
walkthrough:
Equate the curve and straight line equations:
$$3x^2 + 2x + 4 = mx + 1 \implies 3x^2 + (2 - m)x + 3 = 0$$

Apply the condition for two distinct real points of intersection (discriminant $\Delta > 0$):
$$(2 - m)^2 - 4(3)(3) > 0 \implies (2 - m)^2 - 36 > 0$$

Factorise the difference of two squares:
$$((2 - m) - 6)((2 - m) + 6) > 0 \implies (-m - 4)(-m + 8) > 0 \implies (m + 4)(m - 8) > 0$$

State the outside solution ranges for the quadratic inequality:
$$m < -4 \quad \text{or} \quad m > 8$$
